memory_candidates.content: When a close-out/re-check task's originating instruction asks to 'downgrade severity' on an errors.json record but the sanctioned writer (errors-append.sh update) only accepts --id/--fix-status/--fixed-date/--fix-task with no severity mutation path, close the record instead of downgrading it (--fix-status fixed --fix-task N). A closed record is out of triage regardless of its historical severity stamp, so closure is a strictly stronger substitute -- it delivers the requested outcome (stop surfacing as open) without widening a flock-disciplined, schema-validated writer's mutation surface for one bookkeeping wish. Always re-read the writer's argument parser at implementation time rather than trusting a plan's prior reading, since the constraint is easy to get wrong from documentation alone.

A documentation claim of byte-identical preservation across a destructive regenerate/restore cycle (e.g. --wipe preserving settings.local.json) should be verified with both a semantic comparison (jq -S recursively sorted then hashed) AND a structural presence check validated against a positive control (synthetic deletion of the exact blocks being checked, confirming the detector actually flags loss) before trusting a zero-result. Lua pairs() iteration nondeterminism across process runs commonly produces byte-level reordering that is easy to mistake for content loss on a naive raw diff; the semantic/structural split cleanly separates 'reordered' from 'dropped'.
